title: Constructible cohomological interval descent on a finite open cover
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and $X=\bigcup_{t\in J}U_t$ a finite open covering [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with inclusions $u_t:U_t\hookrightarrow X$. The empty family $J=\varnothing$ is allowed when $X=\varnothing$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and derived open restriction $Lu_t^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $F\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be arbitrary, with no prior boundedness or etale-origin assumption. Then for any integers $r\leq s$: if $Lu_t^*F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(U_t,A)$ for every $t\in J$, then $F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(X,A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. No Tor hypothesis is imposed. In particular, if each restriction $Lu_t^*F$ is bounded constructible with its own finite cohomological interval, then $F$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

For $X=\varnothing$ one has $F=0$, so the implication holds for every displayed interval.

proof.text: First record the geometric finiteness needed for the partitions. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. It is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. For finite-type schemes over a field, [def-weil-constructible-subset] records that every locally closed subset is constructible and every open is retrocompact. For each $x\in X$ choose $t$ with $x\in U_t$ and an affine open neighbourhood $W_x\subset U_t$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Quasi-compactness gives a finite affine subcover $W_a$ of $X$, indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}N$, with a chosen containment $W_a\subset U_{t(a)}$. No separatedness of $X$ or affineness of intersections is used.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); properties.tex Tag 01OY; schemes.tex Tag 01IT; topology.tex Tag 005L.

proof.text: For any open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$ and identifies their constant coefficient rings. By [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], the module inverse image $v^*$ is localized restriction. This functor is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Thus termwise restriction of an arbitrary representative complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes $Lv^*F$, with no boundedness assumption. Since exactness preserves kernels, images and their quotient, the cohomology formula of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives $\mathcal H^i(F)|_V\cong\mathcal H^i(Lv^*F)$ for every integer $i$. The same assertion applies to open immersions between any of the charts and local strata.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products); sites-modules.tex Section 03DH and Tag 03DJ; kernels/images formula for cohomology.

proof.text: The family $\{U_t\to X\}$ is a covering in the small pro-etale site. Indeed its arrows are open immersions, hence weakly etale; for every affine open $V\subset X$, refine the open cover $\{V\cap U_t\}$ by affine opens and choose a finite subcover of the quasi-compact $V$. This is exactly the covering criterion of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. If $i\notin[r,s]$, the hypotheses and Step 2 make every restriction of $\mathcal H^i(F)$ to $U_t$ zero. The sheaf-vanishing assertion in [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative](1) therefore gives $\mathcal H^i(F)=0$. This uses covering-family detection, which is valid for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves, and does not use detection by geometric stalks.

source.place: Definition of the small pro-etale covering families; covering-locality argument of blueprint thm-pur-general-admissibility, Step 4.

proof.text: We spell out a sheaf transport fact used for the partitions. Let $L$ be a locally constant $A$-module sheaf with finite geometric stalks on a scheme $T$. Choose trivializing covering members $T_j\to T$ and constant values $M_j$ by [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Discard empty members. On each remaining member $r_j:T_j\to T$ choose a geometric point. Since $T_j\to T$ is an object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction](1),(3) identifies the localized restriction $L|_{T_j}$ of [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] with the inverse image $r_j^{-1}L$, as abelian sheaves and as $A$-module sheaves. The inverse-image stalk isomorphism [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk], together with the underlying abelian inverse-image identification of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], then identifies the stalk of $L|_{T_j}$ there with a finite stalk of $L$. By [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk], that same stalk is $M_j$; hence $M_j$ is finite. Thus the chosen trivialization has finite module models. For any scheme morphism $h:Z\to T$, [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant] provides the base-changed trivialization of $h^*L$ with the same finite $M_j$. Its stalks are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-model-stalks]. Consequently pullback preserves local constancy with finite stalks. If $T$ or $Z$ is empty the assertion is vacuous. No conservativity assertion about stalks is involved.

source.place: Tag 093R (lemma-pullback-locally-constant); sites.tex Tag 00Y8(3), sheafification does not change stalks; proetale.tex Tag 0993, classical points.

proof.text: Fix $i\in[r,s]$. By [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] each $\mathcal H^i(Lu_t^*F)$ admits a finite partition of $U_t$ by constructible locally closed immersed subschemes on which it is locally constant with finite stalks. For $W_a\subset U_{t(a)}$, intersect that partition with $W_a$: more precisely take the open inverse image of $W_a$ in each stratum scheme, so there are actual morphisms to those strata. These are disjoint locally closed subschemes covering $W_a$ and are constructible by the Noetherian-space clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Step 2 identifies the sheaf being restricted with $\mathcal H^i(F)|_{W_a}$; Step 4 preserves its local constancy and finite stalks on the intersected strata. For these identifications inverse images along composite scheme morphisms compose: [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] gives this for underlying abelian sheaves, and [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] gives the same compatibility with the fixed $A$-action.

source.place: Tag 095E (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), finite affine refinement; topology.tex Tag 005L; sites.tex Tag 03CB.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core] to the finite affine cover $W_a$ and the partitions of Step 5. Its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses hold by Step 1. It gives a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification $X=\coprod_c S_c$ and, for each $c$, an actual factorization $S_c\to T_{a,b}\to W_a\to X$ through one of the chart strata. Pulling $\mathcal H^i(F)$ along this factorization identifies its restriction to $S_c$ with the pullback of its locally constant finite-stalk restriction to $T_{a,b}$. Here composition for underlying abelian inverse images is [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], and the coefficient-compatible version is [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Step 4 shows that this pullback is locally constant with finite stalks. Hence $\mathcal H^i(F)$ has exactly the finite global partition required by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. This applies separately to each of the finitely many $i\in[r,s]$; a common stratification across all degrees is not required by that definition.

source.place: Tag 095E (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), implication (2) to (3): finite global immersed refinement.

proof.text: Step 3 gives vanishing outside the finite integer interval $[r,s]$, and Steps 5--6 give constructibility in every remaining degree. Zero cohomology sheaves are constructible as well: on the single stratum $X$ they are the constant module sheaf with value $0$. By [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] this says $F\in D_c^b(X,A)$, and by [def-weil-constructible-intervals] it says $F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(X,A)$. This conclusion has used no Tor-amplitude condition.

source.place: Definition of constructible sheaves, Tag 099Y; blueprint definitions of bounded constructible complexes and cohomological intervals.

proof.text: For the asserted consequence assume first $J\ne\varnothing$. Choose a finite interval $[r_t,s_t]$ for each bounded constructible restriction (choose $[0,0]$ when the restriction is zero), and put $r=\min_t r_t$, $s=\max_t s_t$. Since $r\le r_t\le s_t\le s$, its cohomology vanishes outside $[r,s]$ by the same vanishing condition of [def-weil-constructible-intervals]; Steps 1--7 apply. If $X=\varnothing$, every object of its small pro-etale site is the empty scheme. The empty family covers the final object by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Clause (1) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] with this empty covering says every module sheaf is zero and every derived morphism is an isomorphism; in particular $0\to F$ is an isomorphism, so $F=0$. The zero object has no nonzero cohomology and the empty partition witnesses constructibility, so it lies in every displayed interval. This proves both the $J=\varnothing$ convention and the bounded-constructible consequence in the empty case.
